anom-c14-51-f9-1779-07-19.summary: The convoy under the King's corvette l'Hirondelle has arrived with troops, victuals and munitions, but the Court's orders were carried out imperfectly (cartridge-pouches forgotten); the repair of the works (to restore their state of 1771) stopped by the abbé Terray and unfinished; no bomb-proof powder magazine; arsenal and port without workmen, timber or sailors; one gunboat sent instead of two and two bad apprentices instead of six good carpenters; gunboats like the one built in 1772 are best; La Serre given the coast service, Desprez and Mingy; the artillery company to be raised by 33 men. Postscript: ships bound for the colony should make a recognition signal off the island.

anom-c14-51-f16-1779-08-29.summary: Report under ten heads on the defence of Cayenne island: gunboats and carpenters, the powder magazine, artillery and the gunners, the new recruits (drunkenness, desertion), a critique of the defence memoir of 'the author worthy of Monseigneur's confidence', the impossibility of guarding every cove (Remontabo, Remire, Mahury) with the troops at hand, the enemy's likely manoeuvres (landing far from the town, the Mahury islet, the Cabassou creek), fire precautions in a wooden town, a retrenchment on the port side and the retreat of the garrison, resistance to the last and then in the country after the project of 1762; orders asked of the minister.

snip.cap: The letter of 19 July 1779 opens under its clear date; “le 13 de ce mois avec” is in clear among the numbers
